message.content: This file implements two flash-geometry-aware write routines for the RP2040 Pico SDK, keeping the address/erase logic separate from the actual NOR flash driver so the production algorithm can be validated against a strict NOR model that rejects 0-to-1 bit transitions, unaligned calls, duplicate erases, and overlapping images. `flash_swap_append` programs one ascending piece of an erase-aligned raw swap image, erasing a sector exactly when a piece first reaches its boundary and padding a short final program page with erased bytes (0xff) so the next piece starts beyond it. `flash_swap_rewrite` rewrites an arbitrary program-page-aligned range through a spare sector: it copies untouched destination pages into the spare, erases the destination sector, then writes back either the original source for the rewritten span or the spare copy for the rest, which lets temporary swap devices keep ordinary block-rewrite semantics without a full erase sector in SRAM. Both functions take a `struct flash_swap_ops` (with `erase`, `program`, and `read` callbacks) and enforce alignment and overflow checks, returning -1 on any violation. They build on the internal `rp2040/dev/flash.h` and `rp2040/dev/flash_swap.h` headers and rely on the RP2040 flash driver for the physical memory operations.

It uses a spare sector to hold a copy of untouched pages so that after the destination erase, all needed pages are available. This lets temporary swap devices retain ordinary block-rewrite semantics without a full erase sector in SRAM.
